title: China-to-Switzerland BESS Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: BESS Fire-Safety and Local Installation Review
rows.target_requirement: Swiss BESS installations commonly require local review by municipal building services, cantonal fire office, insurer, and project owner in addition to CE-aligned technical documentation. Swiss authorities usually do not publish a single mandatory nationwide stand-alone national BESS fire certificate; acceptance is handled through site-specific fire dossier review in the project pathway.
target_standards: Cantonal fire-prevention and building-coordination requirements where applicable
Local fire office, municipality, insurer, and project-owner fire-safety review
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly relies on GB 44240-2024, GB/T 36276-2023, and GB/T 36558 plus project fire-design review for stationary energy storage. These documents can support Swiss-side preparation but do not replace Swiss municipal or cantonal fire dossier and local authority expectations.
rows.gap: Prepare a Swiss site-specific fire dossier with installation class, thermal runaway mitigation, fire detection and suppression layout, ventilation and gas-management strategy, spacing, access route, emergency shutdown, runoff and contamination controls where relevant, commissioning tests, and multilingual emergency instructions matching the Swiss project team.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where local authorities, municipality, insurer, and project owner require site acceptance; no national single-purpose BESS fire certificate is stated as a general statutory shortcut.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or project-specific for Chinese domestic review; Chinese fire reports are not direct Swiss municipality or cantonal acceptance proof.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Product fire reports are not a standalone Swiss site-acceptance basis. Include local dossier files for cantonal fire and municipal coordination before commissioning.

source.publisher: Swiss Federal and cantonal safety/regulatory bodies

rows.requirement: Swissgrid Interconnection and Market/Storage Participation Review
rows.target_requirement: Switzerland usually requires project-level grid-connection coordination and market-path classification for BESS installations. Swissgrid and the local distribution operator usually review point of connection, capacity, protection logic, metering, protection settings, and control requirements before energisation.
target_standards: Swissgrid interconnection and technical connection conditions
ElCom Electricity Supply framework and connection rules where applicable
Utility interconnection review and acceptance documentation
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB/T 36558-2023 and related utility interconnection procedures for electrochemical storage project planning and grid studies. These materials support technical comparison but cannot replace Swissgrid and Swiss local network-operator project approval.
china_standards: China State Grid / China Southern Power Grid interconnection materials
rows.gap: Exporters should confirm Swiss project categorisation (storage, controllability, curtailment, dispatch role), confirm local operator requirements, and align anti-islanding, over/under-voltage and frequency logic, protection selectivity, metering, remote-control, and commissioning evidence before site energisation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for grid-connected BESS in Swiss regulated projects where Swissgrid and local operator approvals apply.
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — China utility interconnection materials are not Swiss grid-approval proof.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Separate product conformity from project interconnection. Swissgrid and local operator path approvals are project-specific and should be completed with approved settings and commissioning records.

rows.requirement: CE-Aligned Electrical Safety and Battery Standards
rows.target_requirement: Switzerland relies on SNV adoption routes for relevant EN/IEC safety standards and applies CE-based product pathways where alignment is recognized. For lithium BESS, TS EN IEC 62619 is commonly used as battery safety evidence and IEC 62933-5-2 is commonly used for system-level evidence in grid-connected applications.
target_standards: Switzerland adoption references under CE-aligned SNV/ElCom frameworks
IEC 62619 battery safety requirements for lithium-ion
IEC 62933-5-2 system safety requirements for BESS
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB 44240-2024 and GB/T 36276-2023 for lithium safety, and GB/T 36558 for system integration evidence. These reports support technical comparison but are not direct Swiss statutory proof by themselves.
rows.gap: Do not treat China GB/T safety reports as sufficient for Switzerland-facing placement. Exporters should build Swiss-facing evidence for model scope, voltage class, thermal design, thermal runaway mitigation, isolation and protection architecture, residual-risk evaluation, and language-ready marking.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where Swiss-facing in-scope BESS documentation requires conformity evidence under CE-aligned and Swissgrid-relevant requirements.
mandatory_status.cn: Not a direct substitute for Switzerland-facing evidence. China baseline is an input only.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep a distinct Swiss-facing evidence pack for TS EN IEC standards and Swiss installation assumptions; do not repurpose China GB/T reports as final placement proof.

rows.target_requirement: Lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped to Switzerland generally need UN Manual of Tests and Criteria Part III subsection 38.3 evidence and the related test summary before air, sea, road, or multimodal transport. Switzerland transport compliance is separate from product conformity and project approval documents.
target_standards: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, Part III, subsection 38.3
rows.china_equivalent: China exporters commonly hold UN 38.3 reports and transport-condition summaries for lithium-battery exports. These reports support shipment planning but must be mapped to Switzerland route, model, chemistry, packaging, and carrier route requirements.
rows.gap: A BESS transport file is not a substitute for Switzerland customs or project clearance. Exporters should prepare model-specific UN 38.3 reports, test summaries, SDS, packing instructions, state-of-charge controls, packaging and charging limits, and carrier-required declarations for the selected route.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where dangerous-goods and transport rules apply for the selected mode and model. Not a substitute for Swiss market-access approvals.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for China and international dangerous-goods transport; does not replace Swiss product, grid, or market approvals.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] UN 38.3 is a Swiss-entry shipment gate, not a Swiss interconnection or conformity gate. Match model and route conditions to shipment documentation and dangerous-goods rules.

source.publisher: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE)
